grammar.meaning: I want to do something.
grammar.explanation: The verb after quiero stays in its basic form: Quiero revisar esto.
grammar.nextReview: Combine with different familiar verbs without a model.

grammar.meaning: Give a reason using because.
grammar.explanation: Quiero revisar esto porque es importante.
grammar.nextReview: Use a new work-related reason, then revisit after a gap.

grammar.meaning: I want / we want.
grammar.explanation: Quiero is first-person singular; queremos is first-person plural. The plural is not quieremos.
grammar.nextReview: Queremos was recalled correctly in a reason clause and Queremos probarla after intervening material. Longer-term retention remains untested.

grammar.meaning: Negate a statement.
grammar.explanation: No es correcto means It isn't correct.
grammar.nextReview: Correctly placed no between an explicit noun subject and está in La función no está lista; adjective correction was separate. Recheck polarity in a new sentence.

grammar.meaning: Say where someone or something is.
grammar.explanation: Use estar for a person's location: Está en Granada. Ser/estar has other uses that have not yet been taught.
grammar.nextReview: Ask for a short location sentence; supply any new forms needed.

grammar.meaning: I speak / he, she or formal you speaks.
grammar.explanation: Hablo un poco means I speak a little.
grammar.nextReview: Hablo recalled without a hint; full un poco de español phrase needed correction. Revisit the complete phrase after a gap.

grammar.meaning: Spelling encountered during practice.
grammar.explanation: Use ñ in español; porque includes r. Check keyboard constraints before treating accent input as a language difficulty. Affirmative sí has an accent. Autorizado is spelled with z. Posibilidad has one s.
grammar.nextReview: Observe naturally; avoid repetitive spelling drills.

grammar.meaning: You can / you may do something.
grammar.explanation: Puedes + infinitive used for permission and requests: Sí, puedes publicarlo and ¿Puedes revisar esto? In session12 the practised tú form was corrected from podes to puedes, then immediately repeated correctly. Full poder conjugation has not been taught.
grammar.nextReview: Puedes used correctly in three prompted requests after the session12 correction; test unaided recall after a longer gap.

grammar.meaning: Use the first-person form for I authorize.
grammar.explanation: Autorizo is the I form of autorizar. Yo can be stated explicitly. Model: Te autorizo a publicarlo.
grammar.nextReview: Recall autorizo in a natural permission exchange; do not treat a translation question as successful learner production.

grammar.pattern: object pronoun + conjugated verb; infinitive + attached pronoun
grammar.meaning: Introductory object-pronoun placement.
grammar.explanation: Te autorizo places te before a conjugated verb. Publicarlo attaches lo after the infinitive. Reviso el documento illustrates a full noun object after the verb. This is not a complete placement rule; other constructions remain to be taught. With querer + infinitive, both Quiero revisarlo and Lo quiero revisar are possible. If lo follows the infinitive it must attach directly; this is not a blanket rule for all verb combinations. In practised expressions with queremos, necesitamos and podemos, both attached and before-conjugated positions are supported; this does not generalize to every verb combination.
grammar.nextReview: Both attached and before-conjugated-verb positions used successfully in a prompted negative transformation. Test choice of position without instructions after a gap.

grammar.meaning: Ask Why not...?
grammar.explanation: Por qué asks why and uses two words with accented qué. Practised ¿Por qué queremos aprender español? and contrasted it with porque for because.
grammar.nextReview: Question structure correct with a start-phrase reminder; accent and punctuation supplied. Recheck after a gap.

grammar.pattern: object lo versus an unstated subject
grammar.meaning: Distinguish publish it from it is correct.
grammar.explanation: Lo represents the object in publicarlo or revisarlo. In the examples no es correcto and es importante, English subject it is left unstated in Spanish. This does not establish a general rule to omit every subject.
grammar.nextReview: Lo recurred as the subject of readiness in Lo no está listo ya. Recheck unstated subject in readiness versus object lo/la after an infinitive.

grammar.pattern: lo for masculine singular objects; la for feminine singular objects
grammar.meaning: Choose the object pronoun to match a thing's grammatical gender.
grammar.explanation: El documento can be replaced by lo as an object; la función by la. Modelled revisarlo/revisarla, then the learner produced Queremos probarla with la función as the stated referent.
grammar.nextReview: Immediate selection succeeded with an explicit referent and verb hint. Recheck without hints after a gap.

grammar.meaning: A little of something; a little Spanish.
grammar.explanation: Use un poco de español for a little Spanish. The learner recalled hablo but omitted de in the noun phrase.
grammar.nextReview: De omitted twice on 10 November, including immediately after a correction. Correct in a cued gap, then Comprendemos un poco de español. Recheck complete chunk without an immediate model.

grammar.meaning: Express purpose: to / in order to.
grammar.explanation: Para comprender = to understand. Compared purpose with a reason clause introduced by porque.
grammar.nextReview: Latest response Necesitamos comprender conversaciones was grammatical but did not express the requested read-to purpose. Leemos para comprender conversaciones modelled; review para + infinitive separately from porque.

grammar.meaning: I read / we read.
grammar.explanation: Leo is the I form; leemos is the we form. Both were supplied, then correctly used in prompted sentences.
grammar.nextReview: Recall forms after a gap and use them in a new sentence.

grammar.meaning: Form the present-tense we form of regular -er verbs.
grammar.explanation: Remove only final -er and retain the stem: leer → leemos, aprender → aprendemos, comprender → comprendemos. Comprender was initially truncated; aprender was then correct after explicit models.
grammar.nextReview: Comprendemos correctly produced twice in this batch, including a next-client-date reply. Recheck aprendemos and other familiar -er forms later.

grammar.meaning: Ask what rather than why.
grammar.explanation: ¿Qué leemos? asks What do we read?; ¿Por qué leemos? asks Why do we read? Word order was correct in practice, while accents and punctuation were supplied; leer was once used for requested aprender.
grammar.nextReview: Ask a new what/why question after a gap and check meaning separately from accent input.

grammar.meaning: We need to do something.
grammar.explanation: Necesitamos leer = We need to read. After a review-it correction, the learner produced Necesitamos publicarlo correctly.
grammar.nextReview: Necesitamos revisarla porque es importante recalled correctly in session12; earlier reviser ending error did not recur. Recheck later.

grammar.meaning: We can / we cannot do something.
grammar.explanation: Podemos leer = We can read. Practised both object-pronoun positions; an affirmative response needed no to match can't before a correct final transfer.
grammar.nextReview: Test affirmative versus negative meaning and keep the requested object without a recent placement instruction.

grammar.meaning: It is ready; report readiness with está.
grammar.explanation: Estar readiness chunk está listo/lista has been correctly used and confused with esto in earlier rounds. All four readiness statements in session12 used the right verb and feminine agreement, with accents supplied. Location and a full ser/estar explanation remain separate learning targets.
grammar.nextReview: Recheck readiness and location in separate familiar contexts after a gap.

grammar.pattern: el logo → listo; la función → lista
grammar.meaning: Match this adjective's singular ending to the noun's grammatical gender.
grammar.explanation: Listo with masculine el logo; lista with feminine la función. Initially selected both correctly after models but later mismatched them in a question and negative sentence.
grammar.nextReview: After the session11 feminine error, correctly used lista in four readiness contexts in session12, including two contrast sentences. Recheck after a longer gap.

grammar.pattern: statement word order with yes/no question intonation and ¿...?
grammar.meaning: Ask yes/no questions about readiness or ability.
grammar.explanation: The practised questions can retain statement word order, with questioning intonation and ¿...?: ¿El logo está listo? and ¿Podemos usarla ya? Other word orders are possible. After an explanation, learner produced three structurally correct questions; opening ¿ was supplied.
grammar.nextReview: Recheck a familiar yes/no question after a gap; all current successes were prompted within one practice sequence.

grammar.pattern: todavía no / ya with readiness or ability
grammar.meaning: Not yet versus already/now in the practised contexts.
grammar.explanation: El logo todavía no está listo = The logo isn't ready yet. La función ya está lista = The feature is ready now. Podemos usarla ya and Ya podemos usarla are both natural here; this is not a universal rule for all adverb positions.
grammar.nextReview: Correct not-yet meaning with sentence-final todavía, then valid initial Todavía no... transformation. Recheck after a gap alongside readiness agreement.

grammar.meaning: Connect contrasting statements with but.
grammar.explanation: Pero = but. Learner correctly produced Queremos usarla, pero todavía no está lista and Está lista, pero no queremos publicarla after introduction.
grammar.nextReview: Recheck one contrasting work sentence after intervening material.

grammar.meaning: Standalone this versus this function in the practised request.
grammar.explanation: In the practised general-this targets, esto stands alone: Revisa esto. Before feminine función, use esta función. Learner had correctly used esta función after a model in session13, but esto before función recurred twice during imperative practice; then correctly chose esta in a gap and used standalone esto in a full command. Esta may itself refer to a known feminine item in other contexts; no complete demonstrative paradigm taught.
grammar.nextReview: Recheck esta función in full sentence production without an immediate model. Latest correct esta was a two-option gap; full Revisa esto was a successful immediate switch.

grammar.meaning: Give practical direct instructions using the familiar tú form.
grammar.explanation: Compared ¿Puedes revisar esto? with Revisa esto. Introduced revisar → revisa, crear → crea, leer → lee. Learner formed all practised command verbs correctly after models, while esto/esta needed separate correction. This rule covers the regular affirmative forms taught; negative, irregular and -ir commands have not been taught.
grammar.nextReview: Recall revisa, crea and lee after intervening material before adding pronoun attachment, negative commands or irregular forms.

practiceUnits.title: I want / we want
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: We want to review this.
practiceUnits.hint: Start with Queremos.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: queremos, without the extra i
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: We want to read, immediately after quieremos was corrected.

practiceUnits.title: Say what isn't correct
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: This isn't correct.
practiceUnits.hint: Put no before es.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: no before the conjugated verb
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: We don't want to publish it; then move lo before queremos.

practiceUnits.title: Test a software feature
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: I want to test this feature.
practiceUnits.hint: Esta función means this feature; this form has not yet been practised.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: probar used for software testing
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Test this request, then test-this-function request answered with the function.

practiceUnits.title: Say how much Spanish you speak
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: I speak a little Spanish.
practiceUnits.hint: I speak = hablo.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: hablo for I speak
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: I speak a little Spanish; hablo correct, de omitted.

practiceUnits.title: A goal and a reason
practiceUnits.prompt: Without a model, give a real work goal and a reason using Quiero ... porque ... .
practiceUnits.modelAnswer: Quiero revisar esto porque es importante.
practiceUnits.hint: Use familiar words; mixed-language attempts are welcome.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Goal plus reason; the model answer is only one possible response.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: I want to review it because it's important.

practiceUnits.title: Give permission
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: Yes, you may publish it.
practiceUnits.hint: You may = puedes.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: puedes + infinitive; affirmative sí has an accent

practiceUnits.title: Learn a little Spanish
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: We want to learn a little Spanish.
practiceUnits.modelAnswer: Queremos aprender un poco de español.
practiceUnits.hint: A little Spanish = un poco de español.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: queremos + aprender, retaining de; lowercase poco and ñ in español
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Hablo and queremos aprender omitted de; cued gap selected de; comprendemos sentence retained complete chunk.

practiceUnits.title: Purpose or reason?
practiceUnits.prompt: Choose porque or para: Queremos probar la función ___ publicarla.
practiceUnits.modelAnswer: Queremos probar la función para publicarla.
practiceUnits.hint: Does the gap introduce a purpose or a reason clause?
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: para + infinitive for purpose; porque + clause for a reason
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Requested We read to understand conversations; grammatical need-to-understand alternative supplied.

practiceUnits.title: Keep the whole -er stem
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: We understand Spanish.
practiceUnits.hint: Keep comprend-; replace only final -er with -emos.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Full comprend- stem correctly recalled in a short-gap sentence; recheck later.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: We understand a little Spanish; then We understand Spanish because we read.

practiceUnits.title: Reading in the present
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: I read to get information.
practiceUnits.hint: I read = leo.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Present form leo/leemos with an appropriate purpose or reason.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: I read to get information; then We read because we want to learn Spanish.

practiceUnits.title: Ask what, rather than why
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: What do we read to learn Spanish?
practiceUnits.hint: What = qué; why = por qué.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Match requested meaning, then question structure and standard spelling.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: What do we want to learn?, then What do we read to learn Spanish?

practiceUnits.title: Say what we need to do
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: We need to publish it.
practiceUnits.hint: We need = necesitamos.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Necesitamos + infinitive; preserve verb ending and requested object.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: We need to review this; standalone esto.

practiceUnits.title: Can or can't, keeping it
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: We can't publish it.
practiceUnits.hint: Keep no for can't and retain the requested object.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Match polarity and meaning; accept both supported pronoun positions.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Requested it answered with grammatical this; then correct publicarla in a transformation.

practiceUnits.title: Ready: listo or lista?
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: The feature isn't ready.
practiceUnits.hint: Match the ending to la función and keep no before está.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Stable está chunk and noun/adjective agreement; assess negation separately.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Feminine not-yet retry, test reason and two contrasts; agreement correct.

practiceUnits.title: Use it in context
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: We can use it because it's ready; it refers to la función.
practiceUnits.hint: Use la for the feminine object.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Keep the object pronoun and readiness adjective matched to the referent.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: We want to use it, but it isn't ready yet; feminine función.

practiceUnits.title: Not yet or ready now?
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: The feature is ready now.
practiceUnits.hint: Ready now uses ya; not yet uses todavía no.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Match time meaning, polarity and noun gender; accept natural ya placement variations.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Can't publish this yet; then initial todavía with feminine publicarla after a model.

practiceUnits.title: Turn a familiar statement into a question
practiceUnits.prompt: Ask: Can we use it now? It refers to la función.
practiceUnits.hint: Keep the familiar word order and use question punctuation.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Question structure and correct object gender; treat supplied accents/punctuation separately.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Is the logo ready? Can we use it? Can we use it now (feature)?

practiceUnits.title: Connect a contrast with pero
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: We want to use it, but it isn't ready yet. It refers to la función.
practiceUnits.modelAnswer: Queremos usarla, pero todavía no está lista.
practiceUnits.hint: But = pero.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Contrast connector, time meaning and consistent feminine reference.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Want to use it but not ready yet; ready but don't want to publish it.

practiceUnits.title: Ask someone to review this
practiceUnits.prompt: Ask: Can you review this?
practiceUnits.hint: Use the familiar tú request form; distinguish standalone this from this function.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Puedes and standalone esto. A grammatical request with different meaning should be acknowledged separately.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Test this; test this function (grammatical the-function response); review this function.

practiceUnits.title: Tell the assistant what to do
practiceUnits.prompt: Tell the assistant: Review this function, please.
practiceUnits.hint: Regular affirmative tú: revisar → revisa; distinguish general this from this function.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Command verb independently assessed from esto/esta and spelling; do not give the model before a recall attempt.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Review this function; create a function; read this; read this function; review this.
